title: Learn Cloud
tagline: From console clicks to architecture you can provision, cost, and defend
description: A three-level curriculum for Cloud Engineers — core services and IAM, then networks and infrastructure as code, then scale, cost, and disaster recovery. AWS is the working provider; the same shapes exist on Azure and GCP.
prerequisites: Linux and networking basics (IPs, DNS, HTTP)
Comfort with a terminal, Git, and reading JSON/YAML
A cloud account with billing alarms; associate-level cert study is useful but not required

levels.title: Cloud Foundations
levels.goal: Map compute, storage, and networking to a simple app and lock it down with IAM

topics.title: Compute, storage, databases
items: VMs vs. containers vs. managed app platforms — when each fits
Object storage vs. block vs. file; buckets and lifecycle
Managed Postgres (RDS/Cloud SQL) vs. a database on a VM

topics.title: The CLI and the console
items: CLI profiles, regions, and never using the root user for daily work
Resource naming and tags from the first resource
CloudTrail/audit logs: who changed what

topics.title: Identity fundamentals
items: Users, roles, policies, and least privilege
Assume-role vs. long-lived access keys
Service identities for apps (instance roles, workload identity)

topics.title: Human access
items: SSO/SSO-backed groups instead of shared passwords
Break-glass admin and why it is logged
Scoping by account/project, not one god account

topics.title: Shared responsibility
items: What the provider patches vs. what you patch
Regions, AZs, and why 'us-east-1 only' is a risk
Well-Architected lenses: reliability, security, cost — at a glance

projects: Three-tier sketch: public HTTP, private app, private database
IAM role for an app that can read one bucket and nothing else
CLI walkthrough: create, tag, and destroy a sandbox resource

levels.title: Networks & Infrastructure as Code
levels.goal: Design a VPC and provision it with Terraform so it is repeatable

topics.title: Network design
items: Public vs. private subnets, NAT, and internet gateways
Security groups and NACLs: allow what you mean
Load balancers, target groups, and health checks

topics.title: Private connectivity
items: Databases and caches with no public IPs
Endpoints/PrivateLink-style access to cloud APIs
DNS inside the VPC (private hosted zones)

topics.title: IaC mechanics
items: Providers, resources, variables, and outputs
Remote state, locking, and why local state does not scale
Plan in CI; human-reviewed apply for production

topics.title: Modules and environments
items: Reusable modules vs. copy-paste stacks
Workspaces or separate state per env/account
Importing a console-created resource once, then never clicking it again

topics.title: Multi-AZ design
items: Spread compute across AZs; multi-AZ databases
Stateless app nodes behind a load balancer
What still fails in one region even with multi-AZ

topics.title: CloudWatch / Azure Monitor / Cloud Monitoring
items: Metrics and alarms on the load balancer and database
Log groups with retention and access control
Budget alerts tied to the same tags as the stack

projects: Terraform a VPC, ALB/NLB, app ASG or equivalent, and private database
No public IP on data stores; documented network diagram
Apply the same module to a second environment with different sizing

levels.title: Scale, Cost & Recovery
levels.goal: Run production-shaped cloud: autoscaling, cost control, and a DR plan you could execute

topics.title: Autoscaling and load
items: Scale on meaningful metrics (queue depth, latency), not vanity CPU
Connection pooling and database limits as the real ceiling
CDN and object storage for static and large downloads

topics.title: Multi-region thinking
items: Active-passive vs. active-active and data gravity
Global DNS failover and health checks
What you cannot fail over if the database is the bottleneck

topics.title: Cost visibility
items: Tags/labels as a contract: team, env, service, cost-center
Budgets, anomaly detection, and rightsizing reports
Savings plans/committed use only after the usage is stable

topics.title: Waste you can kill
items: Idle NAT, unattached volumes, leftover load balancers
Log and snapshot retention that quietly dominates the bill
Fintech/SACCO: isolate prod accounts so a sandbox cannot surprise finance

topics.title: RPO/RTO in practice
items: Backup, PITR, and restore drills — not only backup jobs
Runbooks: who declares DR, DNS cutover, and data-loss communication
Game-day restore of a database into an isolated account

topics.title: Guardrails
items: SCP/org policies or equivalent: deny public buckets, require encryption
Encryption at rest and in transit as default
Secrets in a manager; rotation for app and human credentials

projects: Autoscaling app stack with budget alerts and a cost dashboard
DR runbook + successful restore drill with measured RPO/RTO
Multi-AZ production VPC module used by two environments
SACCO-style account layout: sandbox vs. prod, mandatory tags, no public data stores
